what_it_does: IBM's Telum II is an enterprise server processor for z/OS systems (mainframes) built using Samsung's advanced 5 nanometer process. It runs at 5.5 gigahertz and integrates eight processor cores on a single chip, achieving high single-thread performance while adding a dedicated accelerator for artificial intelligence workloads and data processing operations. The processor includes massive on-chip memory caches (360 megabytes total, a 40 percent increase) to reduce memory bottlenecks, and supports coherent multi-drawer configurations where up to 32 chips can be connected together through interconnects while maintaining cache consistency across the system.
